Messages.Author: jeff...@pacbell.net
Messages.Body:
We have a situation in a JOL game and I wanted some clarification on
what should happen:

Meths: A > B > C > D > E

Meth A has been bled by Meth E. Meth B Major Boon'd the bleed.
Meth A is down to 1 pool. Meth B controls the Curse of Nitocris. Meth E
controls the Edge.

Meth A bleeds Meth B for 1.
If the bleed is successful and Meth B burns the Major Boon, what
happens?

Is Meth A instantly ousted?
If so, what happens to the Edge and Curse? I presume nothing.

If there is a window of time for the Edge/Curse movement, if Meth A
takes the Edge, can they move the Curse (or are they getting the Edge
after being ousted)?

Anyway, I think that no movement of Edge or Curse would occur, but I
did want confirmation of this. Thanks.

Jeff

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
jeff...@pacbell.net wrote:
> We have a situation in a JOL game and I wanted some clarification on
> what should happen:
>
> Meths: A > B > C > D > E
>
> Meth A has been bled by Meth E. Meth B Major Boon'd the bleed.
> Meth A is down to 1 pool. Meth B controls the Curse of Nitocris. Meth E
> controls the Edge.
>
> Meth A bleeds Meth B for 1.
> If the bleed is successful and Meth B burns the Major Boon, what
> happens?

A burns 1 pool (for the bleed), assuming no one else reduces the amount
of the bleed.

> Is Meth A instantly ousted?

Yes.

> If so, what happens to the Edge and Curse? I presume nothing.

The bleed is successful for 1 or more, so the Edge is given to A, who
is ousted, so goes uncontrolled. (parallel to the "Cards whose control
is given to an ousted Methsuelah are burned" case, [RTR 21-FEB-1996])

The Curse stays put, since a new Methuselah did not get control of the
Edge.

Messages.Author: Salem
Messages.Body:
jeff...@pacbell.net wrote:

> If there is a window of time for the Edge/Curse movement, if Meth A
> takes the Edge, can they move the Curse (or are they getting the Edge
> after being ousted)?

Note that it is the Methuselah with the curse who gets to move it, not
the methuselah getting the edge. The ambiguous "they" above made me feel
the need to clarify this.
